highlights.title: A step toward defining the Standard Model on a lattice
highlights.summary: Explore a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model and how GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof.
body: In the first guest post on our science blog, physicist Nathaniel Craig, a visiting scientist at OpenAI, describes how he worked with GPT‑6 Astra on a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model. Craig leads the particle theory group at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics.

I had a strategy for tackling this problem, but had not been able to prove that it worked in all the cases it needed to cover. Astra helped turn that strategy into a construction and took the lead in developing the detailed proof. To explain what we did, it helps to start with what is missing from our existing description of the Standard Model.
points: Explore a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model and how GPT-6 Astra helped turn the idea into a detailed proof.

highlights.title: Our new blog for science
highlights.summary: The OpenAI science blog shares new findings, practical methods, and firsthand accounts from researchers using AI to advance scientific discovery.
body: We’re starting the OpenAI science blog to give scientists and academic researchers a place to share what they’re discovering with AI and how they’re doing the work. Our mission is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity, and accelerating scientific discovery is one of the most impactful ways we can work toward that goal.
Research and discoveries: New scientific results and updates on ongoing research from OpenAI, our collaborators, and the broader scientific community.

Methods and practical guidance: Examples of how scientists use our models for tasks such as scientific computing, data analysis, exploring literature, and planning experiments. We’ll share approaches others can adapt, including how to check the work and where a method falls short.

Perspectives from the scientific community: Firsthand accounts from researchers using AI, what they are learning, and how these capabilities are affecting their disciplines. We’ll also discuss open questions about scientific practice and how to make these tools useful to more people.

highlights.title: All 10 Zelda: Ocarina of Time Bosses, Ranked From Worst to Best
highlights.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time brought every great aspect back from the original version — including its iconic boss fights. From fire-breathing dragons to giant spiders to wicked witches, Ocarina of Time features a diverse lineup of boss battles that adds to every dungeon's unique charm…
body: Many of the bosses force players to use the items obtained in their respective dungeons in Ocarina of Time. But overall, many of them feature such clever designs and battles that have made exploring the dungeons worthwhile. In fact, the bosses are so great that Nintendo has allowed players to fight them again in the remake’s Hall of Fallen Foes.

No boss in this game is the same, and some are far better than others. While Zelda fans may be familiar with them from the original game, some of the bosses have been given some enhancements in the remake. So now, here are all the bosses in Ocarina of Time ranked from worst to best.

Nintendo made the Water Temple in Ocarina of Time much easier and enjoyable for gamers in the remake, but the aquatic boss fight still feels dry. There’s nothing visually noteworthy about Morpha, as it’s essentially a giant blob of water with an amoeba inside it. The player simply has to use the Longshot to pull out Morpha’s core and strike it repeatedly. Though the remake gives Morpha some more dynamic attacks, many can agree that Dark Link was a much more interesting battle in the Water Temple.

highlights.title: How sensitive data from Centrelink and other Australian agencies may have been fed to Palantir software
highlights.summary: Exclusive: Personal information of Centrelink clients and childcare workers is among data shared with ACIC, which uses US tech company’s software. The personal information of Centrelink customers, taxpayers and childcare workers is among a trove of sensitive data that may be ending up in Palantir’s…
body: As Guardian Australia reported in September, Palantir’s software is used by the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission (ACIC) as part of the multi-agency fraud fusion taskforce, which was established in 2022 with the goal of targeting fraud in government payments from the national disability insurance scheme, childcare and welfare.

New documents, released under freedom of information requests, reveal the extent to which at least 10 government agencies share sensitive data with the taskforce, which could be fed into Palantir’s software.

The controversial US tech company, co-founded by the Donald Trump-aligned billionaire Peter Thiel, has clients including the Israeli military and US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) that use the software to analyse vast amounts of data.

While the company has insisted it has no access to the data clients enter into the software, the Greens leader, David Shoebridge, has led calls for a ban on Palantir contracts with the Australian government.

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.

Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.

Hamilton’s Mission 44 foundation established in 2021 has published a new report, titled Igniting Inclusion, five years after the groundbreaking assessment made by the Hamilton commission to investigate and address the lack of representation of black people, women and those from lower‑income backgrounds in motorsport.

Enter Anjli Mohindra, who is reprising her role as Rani Chandra. The Big Finish 12-episode audio drama series will be released in August 2027, and is titled Doctor Who — The Tenth Doctor and Rani.

Mohindra first stepped into the world of Who in the 2008 Doctor Who spinoff, The Sarah Jane Adventures. Rani, alongside Luke Smith, Clyde Langer, and the robot dog K9, helped former Doctor companion Sarah Jane Smith in protecting Earth from alien threats. Curious and passionate, Sarah Jane took Rani under her wing and helped her learn journalism. After Sarah Jane's death, Rani would go on to become one of the best journalists in the world.

highlights.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
highlights.summary: Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are.
body: The study will be conducted through a new app where participants can ask health questions and rate the responses.

The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today, with Apple looking for up to 200,000 people to contribute. Participants 21 and older must be based in the US, and although the app doesn’t use Apple Intelligence, it does require an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 26 or later.

Study participants can use the app to ask health-related questions and receive easily understandable responses with links to peer-reviewed clinical sources. The app relies on text-based prompts, and while dictation is an option using the iOS keyboard, the app isn’t integrated with Siri or Apple Intelligence.

body: Following revelations about Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy Congress wants to crack down.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also sent letters to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the committee.

Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act, first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are receiving renewed interest. While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters. Johnson has also said that he personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

highlights.title: Halo Defined a Generation of LAN Parties — Then It Killed Them
highlights.summary: So old, in fact, that the upcoming 25th anniversary of the Xbox and Halo: Combat Evolved immediately made me think about the LAN parties my brother and I used to host in middle and high school.
body: Few things make me feel like Matt Damon aging in that endlessly memed shot from Saving Private Ryan quite like seeing a formative part of my childhood turn 25. My hair is thinner. My bad vision is somehow even worse. My eyes look tired. I am old.

At some point during my obsession with Halo, I discovered that you could connect four Xbox consoles through a router and play across four TVs. You didn’t even need an internet connection. For some mysterious reason, my parents already owned several Ethernet cables that were dozens of feet long. Maybe they’d wanted a wired connection in every room. Maybe there was a sale. Whatever the explanation, we had the infrastructure.

Thus began an exciting era during which my parents kindly allowed us to host massive, very loud sleepovers dedicated exclusively to playing Halo. The living room served as the Nexus. Yes, I called it that, because I’m a huge nerd. It had the biggest screen, the best seating, and the spare router we used to connect everything.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
highlights.summary: Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies including General Atomics.
body: Bharat Semi, an Indian semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as it seeks to win customers in the United States and elsewhere.

The investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon. Its image sensors, however, remain under development, with the startup targeting its initial commercial production in 2027.

India has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S. companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. The country, however, has yet to establish itself as a major chip manufacturing hub. Meanwhile, the AI boom is also giving Indian startups such as Bharat Semi an opportunity to develop specialized chips for global markets.

highlights.title: Reports of AI-related child sexual abuse material rise 8,400% in two years, data shows
highlights.summary: Calls for governments to recognise sexual exploitation of children as preventable public health emergency. Reports of artificial intelligence being used to sexually exploit children have risen by more than 8,400% in two years, research has found.
body: A report by the Edinburgh-based Childlight – Global Child Safety Institute says AI-related child abuse material, including deepfakes using “nudify apps”, had risen from about 4,700 in 2023 to more than 400,000 in 2025.
The images, although fake, can be used to blackmail children to demand money or more images.
The research examined reports of material by tech companies to the US-based organisation the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.
Prof Debi Fry, the global director of data at Childlight, said the findings showed the “shocking” level of child sexual exploitation.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang Reportedly Weighing Return as Nvidia CEO With Allies
highlights.summary: Jensen Huang has reportedly had discussions with his allies about a potential return as Nvidia's CEO just days after reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and multiple employees led to his resignation.
body: Information on what is only the latest unexpected turn in a tangled web of updates for the tech giant came from a new Financial Times report. It stated that Huang has had private discussions with confidantes about the possibility of his reinstatement, as some Nvidia employees and minds from across Silicon Valley call for his return.

Nvidia has found itself in headlines in the tech world for the wrong reasons the last week. The company's board announced it had launched an independent investigation into Huang just seven days ago as it looked into allegations that he had been unfaithful to his wife with an individual the U.S. government believed to be a spy working for the Chinese government. At the time, Nvidia said it "had no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised" but continued with the investigation to "examine all available information."

highlights.title: Hopkins’ late stunner sends Kansas City past Gotham and into NWSL final
highlights.summary: Hopkins’ 89th-minute volley seals dramatic 2-1 upset. Bethune scores stunning free kick against top seeds. Current to face Washington Spirit for first NWSL title. After a week dominated by a headline-grabbing stadium imbroglio, Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current finally got down to the vital…
body: Haley Hopkins delivered the knockout blow at the death, hitting an 89th-minute volley off the crossbar and in to seal a 2-1 upset that shattered Gotham FC’s bid for the league’s first-ever treble. Paired with Croix Bethune’s first-half free-kick stunner, the late winner sent fourth-seeded Kansas City past the NWSL Shield and in-season Challenge Cup winners into a championship showdown in six days against the Washington Spirit.

On a windswept afternoon where unyielding gusts undercut the warmth of a near-cloudless 50F sky, a physical opening stretch produced six fouls in the first eight minutes before either side threatened. Gotham recorded the first shot after 12 minutes when Jaedyn Shaw ran onto a Guro Reiten pass and missed wide right. Kansas City answered three minutes later, with Malawian star Temwa Chawinga firing wide left from the center of the area.

highlights.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
highlights.summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff Sunday, a crushing setback that will ripple across all sectors of the US space industry.
body: The Vulcan rocket is on contract to launch roughly half of the US military’s national security space missions in the next few years, and Sunday’s mission was the first of 38 Vulcan launches booked by Amazon to build out its network of broadband Internet satellites aimed at competing with SpaceX’s Starlink. Sunday’s failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period of time.

Vulcan is no stranger to close calls, having overcome failures with its strap-on solid rocket boosters on two of its four previous flights. In each case, the rocket corrected for those problems and continued into orbit to deploy its payloads. The incidents trigged months-long reviews and investigations before ULA could resume Vulcan flights.

Sunday’s launch succumbed to a different kind of failure. The six solid rocket boosters appeared to perform well in the first two minutes after Vulcan’s liftoff from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, at 12:40 pm EDT (17:40 UTC).

highlights.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
highlights.summary: Apple's new app for a study will answer everyday medical questions
body: Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people.

The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.

The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys.

highlights.title: Greaves out of Grand Slam despite win over Zonneveld
highlights.summary: Beau Greaves' win over Niels Zonneveld is in vain as she is knocked out of the Grand Slam of Darts because of Saturday's heavy defeat by Luke Littler.
body: Beau Greaves was eliminated from the Grand Slam of Darts at the group stage despite ending her campaign with a win over Niels Zonneveld in Wolverhampton.
Greaves, 22, beat Dutchman Zonneveld 5-3 but it was not enough to keep her in the competition after Saturday's heavy defeat by Luke Littler.
The three-time women's world champion fought back impressively from 3-1 down, winning three consecutive legs to take the lead in the best-of-five match.
She missed two match darts in a tense final leg but 28-year-old Zonneveld could not capitalise, failing to take out 154 before Greaves finished with double eight to seal the victory.

highlights.title: Xbox Confirms Project Helix Is 'a Console Capable of Playing Games From Your PC'
highlights.summary: Xbox has confirmed Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC."
body: Microsoft unveiled a slew of details about its past, present, and future with the surprise publication of the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. It's all part of surprise festivities meant to help celebrate 25 years of Xbox, and it also happens to have revealed more information about Project Helix than we've received in some time.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has called the next-gen project a "family of devices" before, and although that language is used again here, vice president of next generation Jason Ronald helped paint a clearer picture. The main idea here is that, through the ups and downs of Xbox's history, many lessons have been learned.

"When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."
points: Xbox has confirmed Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC."

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

highlights.summary: Hint: The shimmering golden dress is from the fall 2007 season.
body: Zendaya is no stranger to shutting down a red carpet—so did you really not expect her to deliver a major fashion serve at the 2026 Governors Awards tonight?

The annual ceremony serves as the official kickoff to the 2027 awards season, so it’s no big surprise that the superstar and her stylist, Law Roach, started things off with a bang this evening—by cultivating a headline-worthy fashion moment worthy of the red carpet. The actor went for gold at the ceremony, choosing a shimmering metallic gown with three-dimensional padding at the hips. And better yet, the striking frock is vintage, too—from the late 2000s. Can you guess the brand and season?

Zendaya and Roach unearthed the fringed column gown from Giles Deacon’s fall 2007 collection, and it feels just as fresh and contemporary today (despite being almost a decade old). Of course. Zendaya and Roach are long known for turning throwback designs into modern-day hits: It’s one of their best fashion tricks. In the past, she has embraced everything from priceless archival Galliano to ’90s Versace to flashy Bob Mackie creations—and she has a knack for always making them feel just as relevant for today.
